title: Restoring memory and attention after a stroke
what: A specialist checks your memory, attention and thinking, then works with you on exercises that help restore them. They teach you how to cope with difficulties in daily life.
why: After a stroke or head injury, if it has become hard to remember, concentrate or plan things.
duration: a session usually takes 45 to 60 minutes, a course takes weeks and months
tell_doctor: What changed after the stroke: memory, attention, speech, mood
What is hardest for you now at home and at work

prepare.title: Sleep
prepare.text: Sleep well the day before - tiredness makes results worse.

prepare.title: Glasses
prepare.text: Bring your glasses and hearing aid, if you use them.

prepare.title: Close person
prepare.text: It is good if a close person comes: they can tell what they have noticed at home.

steps: The specialist asks you and your close ones questions
Gives tasks: remember words, find shapes, solve simple problems
Makes a plan of sessions from the results
In sessions you train memory and attention
You are taught to use cues: lists, alarms, a calendar
You are given tasks to do at home
feel: The tasks can be hard and tiring - take breaks
It can be frustrating when something does not work - this is normal
after: Do the homework a little every day
Keep a regular routine of sleep and rest
Use lists and reminders - there is no shame in it
red_flags: Sudden weakness in an arm or leg, a drooping face or trouble speaking - call your local emergency number
A sudden worsening of memory or confusion - call your doctor

faq.q: Will memory recover after a stroke?
faq.a: Often it recovers partly or noticeably, especially in the first months. Regular sessions help.
A little. But sessions planned by a specialist work better.

reminders.text: Neuropsychologist session today. Take your glasses and a notebook.
